**Sabrina's Slowbro** (Japanese: **ナツメのヤドラン**_Natsume's Yadoran_) is a [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(TCG) "Psychic (TCG)") Stage 1 Pokémon card. It is part of the [Gym Heroes](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Heroes_(TCG) "Gym Heroes (TCG)") expansion.

## Trivia

Although [Slowpoke](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Slowpoke_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Slowpoke (Pokémon)") only evolve into [Slowbro](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Slowbro_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Slowbro (Pokémon)") starting at level 37, Sabrina's Slowbro is level 29.

### Origin

Naptime's Japanese name is that of Power Nap, an [Ability](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ability "Ability") introduced in [Pokémon Conquest](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Conquest "Pokémon Conquest") that [Slowbro](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Slowbro_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Slowbro (Pokémon)") cannot have.

**Sabrina's Slowbro** (Japanese: **ナツメのヤドラン**_Natsume's Yadoran_) is a [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(TCG) "Psychic (TCG)") Stage 1 Pokémon card. It is part of the [Gym Heroes](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Heroes_(TCG) "Gym Heroes (TCG)") expansion.

## Trivia

Although [Slowpoke](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Slowpoke_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Slowpoke (Pokémon)") only evolve into [Slowbro](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Slowbro_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Slowbro (Pokémon)") starting at level 37, Sabrina's Slowbro is level 29.

### Origin

Naptime's Japanese name is that of Power Nap, an [Ability](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Ability "Ability") introduced in [Pokémon Conquest](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Conquest "Pokémon Conquest") that [Slowbro](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Slowbro_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Slowbro (Pokémon)") cannot have.

Actually Gym Heroes had Sabrina's Abra etc. Let's find Sabrina's Gengar in Gym Heroes? We must check. There might be no Gengar in Gym Heroes. We have Sabrina's Gengar in Gym Challenge only.

Also we have Sabrina's Slowbro (Gym Heroes) but has weakness Psychic, so fails.

**Sabrina's Alakazam** (Japanese: **ナツメのフーディン**_Natsume's Foodin_) is a [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(TCG) "Psychic (TCG)") Stage 2 Pokémon card. It was first released as part of the [Gym Challenge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Challenge_(TCG) "Gym Challenge (TCG)") expansion.

## Release information

In Japan, this card was released in the [Yamabuki City Gym](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Yamabuki_City_Gym_(TCG) "Yamabuki City Gym (TCG)")[Theme Deck](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Theme_Deck_(TCG) "Theme Deck (TCG)"). It was later released in the [Gym Challenge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Challenge_(TCG) "Gym Challenge (TCG)") expansion, having been previously reprinted in the Japanese [Challenge from the Darkness](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Challenge_from_the_Darkness_(TCG) "Challenge from the Darkness (TCG)") expansion.

## Trivia

### Origin

[Gym Leader](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader")[Sabrina](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Sabrina "Sabrina") owns an [Alakazam](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Alakazam_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Alakazam (Pokémon)") in [Pokémon Red and Blue](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Blue_Versions "Pokémon Red and Blue Versions").

**Sabrina's Alakazam** (Japanese: **ナツメのフーディン**_Natsume's Foodin_) is a [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(TCG) "Psychic (TCG)") Stage 2 Pokémon card. It was first released as part of the [Gym Challenge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Challenge_(TCG) "Gym Challenge (TCG)") expansion.

## Release information

In Japan, this card was released in the [Yamabuki City Gym](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Yamabuki_City_Gym_(TCG) "Yamabuki City Gym (TCG)")[Theme Deck](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Theme_Deck_(TCG) "Theme Deck (TCG)"). It was later released in the [Gym Challenge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Challenge_(TCG) "Gym Challenge (TCG)") expansion, having been previously reprinted in the Japanese [Challenge from the Darkness](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Challenge_from_the_Darkness_(TCG) "Challenge from the Darkness (TCG)") expansion.

## Trivia

### Origin

[Gym Leader](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader")[Sabrina](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Sabrina "Sabrina") befriends a [Haunter](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Sabrina%27s_Haunter "Sabrina's Haunter") in [_Pokémon the Series: The Beginning_](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Original_series "Original series"). [Nightmare](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Nightmare_(move) "Nightmare (move)") is a [move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Move "Move") introduced in the [Generation II](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Generation_II "Generation II")[Pokémon games](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_games "Pokémon games") that [Haunter](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Haunter_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Haunter (Pokémon)") can learn.

**Sabrina's Gengar** (Japanese: **ナツメのゲンガー**_Natsume's Gangar_) is a [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(TCG) "Psychic (TCG)") Stage 2 Pokémon card. It is part of the [Gym Heroes](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Heroes_(TCG) "Gym Heroes (TCG)") expansion.

**Sabrina's Hypno** (Japanese: **ナツメのスリーパー**_Natsume's Sleeper_) is a [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(TCG) "Psychic (TCG)") Stage 1 Pokémon card. It was first released as part of the [Gym Challenge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Challenge_(TCG) "Gym Challenge (TCG)") expansion.

Invigorate

よみがえらせる

Choose 1 Basic Pokémon in any player's discard pile. Put it onto that player's Bench. Put a number of damage counters on that Pokémon equal to half its HP (rounded down to the nearest 10). _(You can't put a Pokémon on a Bench that's full.)_

Pendulum Curse

ふりこののろい

20×

Flip a number of coins equal to the number of damage counters on the Defending Pokémon. This attack does 20 damage times the number of heads.

## Release information

In Japan, this card was released in the [Yamabuki City Gym](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Yamabuki_City_Gym_(TCG) "Yamabuki City Gym (TCG)")[Theme Deck](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Theme_Deck_(TCG) "Theme Deck (TCG)"). It was later released in the [Gym Challenge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Challenge_(TCG) "Gym Challenge (TCG)") expansion, having been previously reprinted in the Japanese [Challenge from the Darkness](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Challenge_from_the_Darkness_(TCG) "Challenge from the Darkness (TCG)") expansion.

**Sabrina's Hypno** (Japanese: **ナツメのスリーパー**_Natsume's Sleeper_) is a [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(TCG) "Psychic (TCG)") Stage 1 Pokémon card. It was first released as part of the [Gym Challenge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Challenge_(TCG) "Gym Challenge (TCG)") expansion.

## Card text

[![Image 36: Psychic](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/e/ef/Psychic-attack.png/20px-Psychic-attack.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_Energy_(TCG) "Psychic")

Invigorate

よみがえらせる

Choose 1 Basic Pokémon in any player's discard pile. Put it onto that player's Bench. Put a number of damage counters on that Pokémon equal to half its HP (rounded down to the nearest 10). _(You can't put a Pokémon on a Bench that's full.)_

[![Image 37: Psychic](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/e/ef/Psychic-attack.png/20px-Psychic-attack.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_Energy_(TCG) "Psychic")[![Image 38: Psychic](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/e/ef/Psychic-attack.png/20px-Psychic-attack.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_Energy_(TCG) "Psychic")

Pendulum Curse

ふりこののろい

20×

Flip a number of coins equal to the number of damage counters on the Defending Pokémon. This attack does 20 damage times the number of heads.

## Release information

In Japan, this card was released in the [Yamabuki City Gym](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Yamabuki_City_Gym_(TCG) "Yamabuki City Gym (TCG)")[Theme Deck](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Theme_Deck_(TCG) "Theme Deck (TCG)"). It was later released in the [Gym Challenge](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Challenge_(TCG) "Gym Challenge (TCG)") expansion, having been previously reprinted in the Japanese [Challenge from the Darkness](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Challenge_from_the_Darkness_(TCG) "Challenge from the Darkness (TCG)") expansion.

**Sabrina's Gengar** (Japanese: **ナツメのゲンガー**_Natsume's Gangar_) is a [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(TCG) "Psychic (TCG)") Stage 2 Pokémon card. It is part of the [Gym Heroes](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Heroes_(TCG) "Gym Heroes (TCG)") expansion.

**Sabrina's Gengar** (Japanese: **ナツメのゲンガー**_Natsume's Gangar_) is a [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(TCG) "Psychic (TCG)") Stage 2 Pokémon card. It is part of the [Gym Heroes](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Heroes_(TCG) "Gym Heroes (TCG)") expansion.

**Pokémon VS** (Japanese: **ポケモンカード★VS**_Pokémon Card★VS_) is the only main expansion of cards from the VS Era of the [Pokémon Card Game](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game "Pokémon Trading Card Game") in Japan. It does not have a main expansion as an English equivalent.

## Information

**Pokémon Card★VS** is the only expansion in the [Pokémon Card Game](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game "Pokémon Trading Card Game") VS Era. It was released on July 19, 2001.

Pokémon Card★VS introduced the classification of [Special Conditions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Special_Condition_(TCG) "Special Condition (TCG)"), which saved the need to reference a number of them in attack or Pokémon Power. [Burned](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Burned_(TCG) "Burned (TCG)") was also added as a Special Condition. It also introduced [Technical Machine cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Technical_Machine_card_(TCG) "Technical Machine card (TCG)"), which allow the Pokémon they are attached to use an attack as specified on the card (a reference to the [TM](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/TM "TM") in the [core series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Core_series "Core series") games).

Pokémon Card★VS was also the first Japanese expansion to utilize a numbering system. The Pokémon were ordered by the sequence in which [players](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Player_character "Player character") encounter the [Gym Leaders](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader") in Pokémon [Gold, Silver](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Gold_and_Silver_Versions "Pokémon Gold and Silver Versions"), and [Crystal Versions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Crystal_Version "Pokémon Crystal Version"), then followed by the sequence in which players battle the [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto")[Elite Four](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Elite_Four "Elite Four"), then [Team Rocket](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Team_Rocket "Team Rocket"), and the [Champion](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champion "Pokémon Champion").

Pokémon Card★VS also introduced an updated card design, which included numerous changes. Firstly, the left and bottom borders have been increased in size. The artwork window is rounded on the left. The Pokémon's species, height and weight were moved to the left, next to its Trainer's headshot. It lacked the [Pokédex](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9dex "Pokédex") entry and the Weakness and Resistance was moved to the right, with the Retreat Cost on the left. The illustrator was moved to the center on the bottom of the card. The set symbol was located on the bottom left of the card. Lastly, the back of the card was changed from the "Pocket Monsters Card Game" to the "Pokémon" design used in international prints.

This was the first Japanese expansion to include [Secret cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Secret_card_(TCG) "Secret card (TCG)") and the first to release [1st Edition](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/1st_Edition_(TCG) "1st Edition (TCG)") prints.

Each booster pack contained 30 cards instead of the usual 10; 12 Pokémon (11 Non Holo and 1 Holo), 4 [Trainer cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Trainer_card_(TCG) "Trainer card (TCG)"), 2 Technical Machine, 11 Basic [Energy cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Energy_card_(TCG) "Energy card (TCG)"), and 1 Holo [Special Energy card](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Special_Energy_card_(TCG) "Special Energy card (TCG)"). Each booster pack cost ¥690 instead of ¥300.

A Psychic/Fighting booster pack contained a Holofoil Pokémon, a Holofoil Special Energy, 6 Fighting Energy, 5 Psychic Energy, 4 Fighting-type Pokémon, 4 Psychic-type Pokémon, 3 Colorless-type Pokémon, 4 Trainer cards, and 2 Technical Machine.

A Water/Fire booster pack contained a Holofoil Pokémon, a Holofoil Special Energy, 6 Water Energy, 5 Fire Energy, 5 Water-type Pokémon, 3 Fire-type Pokémon, 3 Colorless-type Pokémon, 4 Trainer cards, and 2 Technical Machine.

A Grass/Lightning booster pack contained a Holofoil Pokémon, a Holofoil Special Energy, 6 Grass Energy, 5 Lightning Energy, 5 Grass-type Pokémon, 3 Lightning-type Pokémon, 3 Colorless-type Pokémon, 4 Trainer cards, and 2 Technical Machine.

There were three random [Half Decks](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Half_Deck_(TCG) "Half Deck (TCG)") released; Fighting & Psychic, Water & Fire, and Grass & Lightning. Each Half Deck contained a random assortment of Pokémon that were exclusive to its type and Colorless-type Pokémon.

Except for [Brock](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock "Brock"), each Owner's cards were illustrated by the same artist; [Atsuko Nishida](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Atsuko_Nishida "Atsuko Nishida") (Falkner), [Kyoko Umemoto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kyoko_Umemoto "Kyoko Umemoto") (Bugsy), [Miki Tanaka](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Miki_Tanaka "Miki Tanaka") (Whitney), [Naoyo Kimura](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Naoyo_Kimura "Naoyo Kimura") (Morty), [Yukiko Baba](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Yukiko_Baba "Yukiko Baba") (Jasmine), [Masako Yamashita](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Masako_Yamashita "Masako Yamashita") (Chuck), [Mitsuhiro Arita](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mitsuhiro_Arita "Mitsuhiro Arita") (Pryce), [Shin-ichi Yoshida](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Shin-ichi_Yoshida "Shin-ichi Yoshida") (Clair), [Etsuya Hattori](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Etsuya_Hattori "Etsuya Hattori") (Lt. Surge), [Asuka Iwashita](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Asuka_Iwashita "Asuka Iwashita") (Sabrina), [Satoshi Ohta](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Satoshi_Ohta "Satoshi Ohta") (Misty), [Motofumi Fujiwara](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Motofumi_Fujiwara "Motofumi Fujiwara") (Erika), [Tomokazu Komiya](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Tomokazu_Komiya "Tomokazu Komiya") (Janine), [Kimiya Masago](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kimiya_Masago "Kimiya Masago") (Blaine), [Kagemaru Himeno](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kagemaru_Himeno "Kagemaru Himeno") (Will), [Toshinao Aoki](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Toshinao_Aoki "Toshinao Aoki") (Koga), [Yuka Morii](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Yuka_Morii "Yuka Morii") (Bruno), [Hajime Kusajima](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hajime_Kusajima "Hajime Kusajima") (Karen), [Hironobu Yoshida](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hironobu_Yoshida "Hironobu Yoshida") (Rocket), and [Aya Kusube](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Aya_Kusube "Aya Kusube") (Lance). ["Big Mama" Tagawa](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/%22Big_Mama%22_Tagawa "\"Big Mama\" Tagawa") illustrated all of the Technical Machine Trainer cards.

Mike Gills of [Wizards of the Coast](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Wizards_of_the_Coast "Wizards of the Coast") claimed to have been informed by [The Pokémon Company](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/The_Pok%C3%A9mon_Company "The Pokémon Company") that Pokémon Card★VS was considered to be a "separate and simpler game" and compared its relation to the TCG with the [Portal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portal_(Magic:_The_Gathering) "wp:Portal (Magic: The Gathering)") sets' relation to [Magic: The Gathering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic:_The_Gathering "wp:Magic: The Gathering").[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_VS_(TCG)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_VS_(TCG)#cite_note-2)

**Pokémon VS** (Japanese: **ポケモンカード★VS**_Pokémon Card★VS_) is the only main expansion of cards from the VS Era of the [Pokémon Card Game](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game "Pokémon Trading Card Game") in Japan. It does not have a main expansion as an English equivalent.

## Information

**Pokémon Card★VS** is the only expansion in the [Pokémon Card Game](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game "Pokémon Trading Card Game") VS Era. It was released on July 19, 2001.

Pokémon Card★VS introduced the classification of [Special Conditions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Special_Condition_(TCG) "Special Condition (TCG)"), which saved the need to reference a number of them in attack or Pokémon Power. [Burned](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Burned_(TCG) "Burned (TCG)") was also added as a Special Condition. It also introduced [Technical Machine cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Technical_Machine_card_(TCG) "Technical Machine card (TCG)"), which allow the Pokémon they are attached to use an attack as specified on the card (a reference to the [TM](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/TM "TM") in the [core series](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Core_series "Core series") games).

Pokémon Card★VS was also the first Japanese expansion to utilize a numbering system. The Pokémon were ordered by the sequence in which [players](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Player_character "Player character") encounter the [Gym Leaders](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader") in Pokémon [Gold, Silver](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Gold_and_Silver_Versions "Pokémon Gold and Silver Versions"), and [Crystal Versions](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Crystal_Version "Pokémon Crystal Version"), then followed by the sequence in which players battle the [Johto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Johto "Johto")[Elite Four](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Elite_Four "Elite Four"), then [Team Rocket](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Team_Rocket "Team Rocket"), and the [Champion](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Champion "Pokémon Champion").

Pokémon Card★VS also introduced an updated card design, which included numerous changes. Firstly, the left and bottom borders have been increased in size. The artwork window is rounded on the left. The Pokémon's species, height and weight were moved to the left, next to its Trainer's headshot. It lacked the [Pokédex](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9dex "Pokédex") entry and the Weakness and Resistance was moved to the right, with the Retreat Cost on the left. The illustrator was moved to the center on the bottom of the card. The set symbol was located on the bottom left of the card. Lastly, the back of the card was changed from the "Pocket Monsters Card Game" to the "Pokémon" design used in international prints.

This was the first Japanese expansion to include [Secret cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Secret_card_(TCG) "Secret card (TCG)") and the first to release [1st Edition](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/1st_Edition_(TCG) "1st Edition (TCG)") prints.

Each booster pack contained 30 cards instead of the usual 10; 12 Pokémon (11 Non Holo and 1 Holo), 4 [Trainer cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Trainer_card_(TCG) "Trainer card (TCG)"), 2 Technical Machine, 11 Basic [Energy cards](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Energy_card_(TCG) "Energy card (TCG)"), and 1 Holo [Special Energy card](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Special_Energy_card_(TCG) "Special Energy card (TCG)"). Each booster pack cost ¥690 instead of ¥300.

A Psychic/Fighting booster pack contained a Holofoil Pokémon, a Holofoil Special Energy, 6 Fighting Energy, 5 Psychic Energy, 4 Fighting-type Pokémon, 4 Psychic-type Pokémon, 3 Colorless-type Pokémon, 4 Trainer cards, and 2 Technical Machine.

A Water/Fire booster pack contained a Holofoil Pokémon, a Holofoil Special Energy, 6 Water Energy, 5 Fire Energy, 5 Water-type Pokémon, 3 Fire-type Pokémon, 3 Colorless-type Pokémon, 4 Trainer cards, and 2 Technical Machine.

A Grass/Lightning booster pack contained a Holofoil Pokémon, a Holofoil Special Energy, 6 Grass Energy, 5 Lightning Energy, 5 Grass-type Pokémon, 3 Lightning-type Pokémon, 3 Colorless-type Pokémon, 4 Trainer cards, and 2 Technical Machine.

There were three random [Half Decks](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Half_Deck_(TCG) "Half Deck (TCG)") released; Fighting & Psychic, Water & Fire, and Grass & Lightning. Each Half Deck contained a random assortment of Pokémon that were exclusive to its type and Colorless-type Pokémon.

Except for [Brock](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Brock "Brock"), each Owner's cards were illustrated by the same artist; [Atsuko Nishida](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Atsuko_Nishida "Atsuko Nishida") (Falkner), [Kyoko Umemoto](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kyoko_Umemoto "Kyoko Umemoto") (Bugsy), [Miki Tanaka](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Miki_Tanaka "Miki Tanaka") (Whitney), [Naoyo Kimura](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Naoyo_Kimura "Naoyo Kimura") (Morty), [Yukiko Baba](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Yukiko_Baba "Yukiko Baba") (Jasmine), [Masako Yamashita](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Masako_Yamashita "Masako Yamashita") (Chuck), [Mitsuhiro Arita](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Mitsuhiro_Arita "Mitsuhiro Arita") (Pryce), [Shin-ichi Yoshida](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Shin-ichi_Yoshida "Shin-ichi Yoshida") (Clair), [Etsuya Hattori](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Etsuya_Hattori "Etsuya Hattori") (Lt. Surge), [Asuka Iwashita](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Asuka_Iwashita "Asuka Iwashita") (Sabrina), [Satoshi Ohta](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Satoshi_Ohta "Satoshi Ohta") (Misty), [Motofumi Fujiwara](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Motofumi_Fujiwara "Motofumi Fujiwara") (Erika), [Tomokazu Komiya](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Tomokazu_Komiya "Tomokazu Komiya") (Janine), [Kimiya Masago](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kimiya_Masago "Kimiya Masago") (Blaine), [Kagemaru Himeno](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Kagemaru_Himeno "Kagemaru Himeno") (Will), [Toshinao Aoki](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Toshinao_Aoki "Toshinao Aoki") (Koga), [Yuka Morii](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Yuka_Morii "Yuka Morii") (Bruno), [Hajime Kusajima](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hajime_Kusajima "Hajime Kusajima") (Karen), [Hironobu Yoshida](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Hironobu_Yoshida "Hironobu Yoshida") (Rocket), and [Aya Kusube](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Aya_Kusube "Aya Kusube") (Lance). ["Big Mama" Tagawa](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/%22Big_Mama%22_Tagawa "\"Big Mama\" Tagawa") illustrated all of the Technical Machine Trainer cards.

Mike Gills of [Wizards of the Coast](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Wizards_of_the_Coast "Wizards of the Coast") claimed to have been informed by [The Pokémon Company](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/The_Pok%C3%A9mon_Company "The Pokémon Company") that Pokémon Card★VS was considered to be a "separate and simpler game" and compared its relation to the TCG with the [Portal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portal_(Magic:_The_Gathering) "wp:Portal (Magic: The Gathering)") sets' relation to [Magic: The Gathering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic:_The_Gathering "wp:Magic: The Gathering").[[1]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_VS_(TCG)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_VS_(TCG)#cite_note-2)

**Sabrina's Xatu** (Japanese: **ナツメのネイティオ**_Natsume's Natio_) is a [Psychic-type](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psychic_(TCG) "Psychic (TCG)") Basic Pokémon card. It is part of the [Pokémon VS](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_VS_(TCG) "Pokémon VS (TCG)") expansion.

## Trivia

### Origin

[Gym Leader](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader")[Sabrina](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Sabrina "Sabrina") owns an [Espeon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Espeon_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Espeon (Pokémon)") in [Pokémon Gold, Silver](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Gold_and_Silver_Versions "Pokémon Gold and Silver Versions"), and [Crystal](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Crystal_Version "Pokémon Crystal Version"). [Psywave](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psywave_(move) "Psywave (move)") is a [move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Move "Move") in the [Pokémon games](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_games "Pokémon games"), though Espeon cannot learn it.

[![Image 37](https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/4/43/Project_TCG_logo.png/80px-Project_TCG_logo.png)](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/File:Project_TCG_logo.png)This article is part of **[Project TCG](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Bulbapedia:Project_TCG "Bulbapedia:Project TCG")**, a [Bulbapedia project](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Bulbapedia:Projects "Bulbapedia:Projects") that aims to report on every aspect of the [Pokémon Trading Card Game](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game "Pokémon Trading Card Game").

## Trivia

### Origin

[Gym Leader](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gym_Leader "Gym Leader")[Sabrina](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Sabrina "Sabrina") owns an [Espeon](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Espeon_(Pok%C3%A9mon) "Espeon (Pokémon)") in [Pokémon Gold, Silver](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Gold_and_Silver_Versions "Pokémon Gold and Silver Versions"), and [Crystal](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Crystal_Version "Pokémon Crystal Version"). [Psywave](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Psywave_(move) "Psywave (move)") is a [move](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Move "Move") in the [Pokémon games](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_games "Pokémon games"), though Espeon cannot learn it.

**Sabrina‑themed Pokémon cards that satisfy all three criteria**  
*(HP ≥ 70 HP, no weakness, and at least one attack that deals 20 – 40 damage)*  

| Set | Card | HP | Weakness | Attack(s) that hit 20‑40 damage* |
|-----|------|----|----------|---------------------------------|
| **Gym Heroes** | Sabrina’s Gengar (card 14/132) | 80 | None | Call of the Night – 40 |
| *Gym Challenge* | Sabrina’s Gengar (card 29/132) | 90 | None | Dark Wave – 20 **and** Shadow Bind – 40 |
| *Gym Challenge* | Sabrina’s Haunter (card 55/132) | 70 | None | Nightmare – 20 **and** Shadow Attack – 30 |
| **Pokémon VS** | – | – | – | – |

\* A card can have multiple attacks; it only needs *at least one* that falls in the 20‑40 damage range. All the listed attacks meet that condition.

**Sources**

1. **Sabrina’s Gengar (Gym Heroes 14)** – Bulbapedia: HP 80, no weakness, second attack (Call of the Night) does 40 damage【source‑Sabrina’s_Gengar_Gym_Heroes_14】.  
2. **Sabrina’s Gengar (Gym Challenge 29)** – Bulbapedia: HP 90, no weakness, attacks Dark Wave (20) and Shadow Bind (40)【source‑Sabrina’s_Gengar_Gym_Challenge_29】.  
3. **Sabrina’s Haunter (Gym Challenge 55)** – Bulbapedia: HP 70, no weakness, attacks Nightmare (20) and Shadow Attack (30)【source‑Sabrina’s_Haunter_Gym_Challenge_55】.  
4. **Sabrina’s Slowbro (Gym Heroes 60)** – Bulbapedia shows a weakness (Psychic)【source‑Sabrina’s_Slowbro_Gym_Heroes_60】, so it does **not** qualify.  
5. **Sabrina’s Hypno (Gym Challenge 56)** – Bulbapedia shows a Psychic weakness【source‑Sabrina’s_Hypno_Gym_Challenge_56】, so it does **not** qualify.

**Pokémon VS**

* The two Sabrina‑related Pokémon cards in the VS set are Sabrina’s Xatu (HP 70, Psychic weakness) and Sabrina’s Espeon (HP 60). Neither meets the “no weakness” or “≥ 70 HP” condition, so **no VS cards** qualify.

**Result**

The only Sabrina‑themed Pokémon cards that meet all three conditions are:

1. **Sabrina’s Gengar – Gym Heroes**  
2. **Sabrina’s Gengar – Gym Challenge**  
3. **Sabrina’s Haunter – Gym Challenge**

No cards from the Pokémon VS set meet the specified criteria.
